HTML export of the improve_disulfide_physicality_with_steering.py interactive Python example with its saved outputs. This page does not run Python code.

To run the example yourself, follow the notebook quickstart.

Guide sampling toward physically realistic structures¶

Sampled structures can contain unrealistic geometry, such as stretched or compressed bonds and overlapping atoms. BioEmu2 can steer sampling away from that geometry with physicality potentials. This notebook samples the C-terminal NTR domain of mouse Meteorin-like protein (PDB 7TLW), first without steering and then with steering. Without steering, most samples fail the physicality checks because their disulfide bonds are too short; the steered samples pass. Measuring how the two helices joined by the disulfides pack shows that steering corrects the disulfides without changing the fold.

A separate example, tilt_a_sample_distribution_with_steering.py, measures how well steering moves a sampled distribution toward a chosen target.

See the steering guide to choose a sampler and the potentials guide for the default physicality potentials.

For installation and hardware requirements, see the notebook quickstart.

In [1]:
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import mdtraj
import numpy as np

from bioemu2 import (
    EDMSampler,
    EmuSession,
    GuidedFKSampler,
    PhysicalityFilterMode,
    PhysicalityReport,
    System,
    check_physicality,
    load_model,
    save_frames,
)
from bioemu2.paths import EXAMPLES_DIR
from bioemu2.physicality import DISULFIDE_BOND_WINDOW
from bioemu2.visualization import view_trajectory

Load the system¶

The domain has two disulfide bonds, Cys20–Cys113 and Cys30–Cys135. PDB import does not read disulfides, so the system file declares them as bonds. Declared bonds are part of the sampled topology, the bond-length steering potential, and the physicality checks.

In [3]:
emu = EmuSession(meteorin_like, model=load_model("bioemu2-preview"), mode="equilibrium")

num_samples = 10
seed = 0
physicality_mode = PhysicalityFilterMode.NO_VIOLATIONS_ALLOWED

check_physicality checks protein bond lengths, including declared disulfides, steric clashes within and between chains, valence, isolated atoms, and duplicate atoms. It does not check ligands or remove frames; it reports whether each frame passed and, for failed frames, the first check that exceeded its threshold. This example uses the strictest preset, no_violations, which rejects a frame with any violation. The default high_quality preset tolerates some other violation types, but also rejects every disulfide outside the accepted S–S range.

In [4]:
def summarize(report: PhysicalityReport) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
    print(f"{int(report.passed.sum())}/{len(report.passed)} samples pass the physicality checks")
    return [
        {"frame": frame, "passes": bool(passed), "failure": reason}
        for frame, (passed, reason) in enumerate(zip(report.passed, report.reasons, strict=True))
    ]


def disulfide_lengths_angstrom(samples: mdtraj.Trajectory) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return SG–SG distances of the disulfide bonds, shape [num_frames, num_bonds]."""
    pairs = [
        [first.index, second.index]
        for first, second in samples.topology.bonds
        if first.name == second.name == "SG"
    ]
    return mdtraj.compute_distances(samples, pairs) * 10.0

Sample without steering¶

EDMSampler runs the reverse diffusion without any potentials.

In [5]:
unsteered_samples: mdtraj.Trajectory = emu.sample(
    num_samples=num_samples, sampler=EDMSampler(), seed=seed
)
unsteered_report = check_physicality(unsteered_samples, physicality_mode, system=meteorin_like)
summarize(unsteered_report)

A disulfide S–S bond is about 2.03 Å long. Without steering, many sampled disulfides are much shorter, which the checks report as bad sidechain bonds or as clashes between the two cysteines.

Sample with physicality steering¶

GuidedFKSampler uses the default physicality potentials unless you pass potentials. They penalize atom overlaps within and between chains, bond lengths and angles outside their reference ranges, and ligand geometry errors. resampling_interval=None disables Feynman-Kac resampling, so each sample is steered only by gradient guidance; this matches the "edm_gd" sampler preset. Guidance evaluates the potentials and their gradients during denoising, so steered sampling takes longer than sampling without steering.

In [7]:
physicality_sampler = GuidedFKSampler(resampling_interval=None)
[type(potential).__name__ for potential in physicality_sampler.potentials]

Steering reduces unrealistic geometry, but it does not guarantee that every sample passes. To keep only samples that pass, select frames with the report: steered_samples[steered_report.passed].

Compare the samples¶

The plot shows every disulfide length in both sets of samples. Filled markers are samples that pass the physicality checks; open markers are samples that fail. The dashed line marks the mean S–S length and the shaded band marks the range of lengths the checks accept. A sample whose disulfides fall inside the band can still fail another check, such as a clash.

In [10]:
reference_disulfide_angstrom = 2.033
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
for row, (samples, report) in enumerate(
    [(unsteered_samples, unsteered_report), (steered_samples, steered_report)]
):
    lengths = disulfide_lengths_angstrom(samples)
    for passed in (True, False):
        frames = report.passed == passed
        values = lengths[frames].ravel()
        jitter = np.random.default_rng(row).uniform(-0.15, 0.15, size=values.shape)
        ax.scatter(
            values,
            row + jitter,
            facecolors=f"C{row}" if passed else "none",
            edgecolors=f"C{row}",
        )
# The y-axis already names each row, so the legend only explains the marker fill
# and reference lines, using gray stand-in markers.
ax.scatter([], [], facecolors="0.4", edgecolors="0.4", label="passes")
ax.scatter([], [], facecolors="none", edgecolors="0.4", label="fails")
ax.axvspan(*DISULFIDE_BOND_WINDOW, color="0.9", zorder=0, label="accepted S–S range")
ax.axvline(reference_disulfide_angstrom, color="black", linestyle="--", label="mean S–S")
ax.set_yticks([0, 1], ["without steering", "with steering"])
ax.set_xlabel("disulfide S–S length (Å)")
ax.set_title("Meteorin-like NTR domain (7TLW) disulfide lengths")
ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc="upper left")
fig.tight_layout()

Check the packing of the helices¶

Steering corrects the disulfide geometry. To check whether it also changes the fold, look at the two helices that the disulfides hold together. The disulfides join Cys20 and Cys30, at either end of the N-terminal helix (N-helix, residues 22–31), to Cys113 and Cys135, on either side of the C-terminal helix (C-helix, residues 117–129). Two quantities describe how the helices pack against each other:

  • the distance between the centers of their Cα atoms;
  • the angle between their axes, each pointing from the first to the last residue of the helix.

If steering moved the bonded cysteines by distorting the fold, both quantities would shift. The deposited 7TLW structure is shown for reference; it does not resolve the first 16 residues of the sampled sequence, so its residues are matched to the sampled sequence before measuring.

In [13]:
n_terminal_helix = range(22, 32)
c_terminal_helix = range(117, 130)


def helix_packing(
    structures: mdtraj.Trajectory, first_residue: int
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return the helix center distance in Å and the interhelix angle in degrees.

    `first_residue` is the 1-based sampled-sequence number of the first residue in
    `structures`.
    """

    def helix_ca(residues: range) -> np.ndarray:
        atoms = [
            structures.topology.select(f"name CA and resid {residue - first_residue}")[0]
            for residue in residues
        ]
        return 10.0 * structures.xyz[:, atoms]

    def helix_axis(ca: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        # The first principal component of the Cα atoms runs along the helix.
        centered = ca - ca.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
        axis = np.linalg.svd(centered, full_matrices=False).Vh[:, 0]
        return axis * np.sign(np.sum(axis * (ca[:, -1] - ca[:, 0]), axis=-1, keepdims=True))

    first, second = helix_ca(n_terminal_helix), helix_ca(c_terminal_helix)
    distance = np.linalg.norm(first.mean(axis=1) - second.mean(axis=1), axis=-1)
    cosine = np.sum(helix_axis(first) * helix_axis(second), axis=-1)
    return distance, np.degrees(np.arccos(np.clip(cosine, -1.0, 1.0)))


crystal = mdtraj.load_pdb("https://files.rcsb.org/download/7TLW.pdb")
crystal_ca = crystal.atom_slice(crystal.topology.select("protein and name CA"))
crystal_sequence = "".join(residue.code for residue in crystal_ca.topology.residues)
sampled_sequence = "".join(residue.code for residue in unsteered_samples.topology.residues)
first_resolved = sampled_sequence.index(crystal_sequence) + 1

packing = {
    "without steering": helix_packing(unsteered_samples, 1),
    "with steering": helix_packing(steered_samples, 1),
    "7TLW": helix_packing(crystal_ca, first_resolved),
}
for source, (distance, angle) in packing.items():
    print(
        f"{source}: median distance {np.median(distance):.1f} Å, median angle {np.median(angle):.0f}°"
    )

without steering: median distance 11.5 Å, median angle 93°
with steering: median distance 11.6 Å, median angle 93°
7TLW: median distance 11.7 Å, median angle 87°
In [14]:
packing_fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
for source, (distance, angle) in packing.items():
    style = {"color": "black", "marker": "*", "s": 250} if source == "7TLW" else {"alpha": 0.7}
    ax.scatter(distance, angle, label=source, **style)
ax.set_xlabel("N-helix to C-helix distance (Å)")
ax.set_ylabel("angle between N-helix and C-helix axes (°)")
ax.set_title("Meteorin-like NTR domain (7TLW) helix packing")
ax.legend(fontsize=8)
packing_fig.tight_layout()

Both sets of samples spread over the same range of distances and angles, around the values of the crystal structure: steering shortens the disulfides to their bonded length without changing how the helices pack.

Save the samples¶

save_frames writes every frame together with the physicality report.

In [15]:
output_dir = Path("outputs/improve_disulfide_physicality_with_steering")
for name, samples, report in [
    ("unsteered", unsteered_samples, unsteered_report),
    ("steered", steered_samples, steered_report),
]:
    output_path = save_frames(samples, output_dir / name, physicality=report)
    print(f"saved {name} samples to {output_path}")
fig.savefig(output_dir / "disulfide_lengths.png", dpi=150)
packing_fig.savefig(output_dir / "helix_packing.png", dpi=150)

saved unsteered samples to outputs/improve_disulfide_physicality_with_steering/unsteered/samples.xtc
saved steered samples to outputs/improve_disulfide_physicality_with_steering/steered/samples.xtc
